result.summary:
Independent gate of docs/agents/design/REQ-030.md, read in full directly (not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary). This is the 6th consecutive design gate and the requirement introduces a genuinely novel interaction mechanism (message-text-as-state-carrier) never used before in this codebase -- given extra scrutiny per the handoff's own steer.

1. ZERO IMPLEMENTATION CODE (exhaustive, all 16 fenced blocks enumerated): lines 133-146 (ParsedWalkinArgs/ParseWalkinArgsResult/parseWalkinArgs -- bare signature, rule stated as a 4-step TABLE at 150-155, not as an if/else body), 157-163 (WalkinFieldValidation/validateWalkinFields -- bare; rule stated as prose at 165-170), 186-188 (normalizePhoneForMatching -- bare signature, rule stated as prose at 190-193), 215-221 (getUserIdByPhone -- bare, ends `;`; query shape described as prose SQL at 223-228, an inline code span not a fenced executable block), 257-283 (WalkinDecisionInput/WalkinDecisionOutcome/decideWalkinOutcome -- bare; the 7-row decision logic is a first-match-wins TABLE at 289-297, matching this codebase's established decideRegistrationOutcome/decideCheckinToggleOutcome/decideQrCheckinOutcome/decideOverrideOutcome convention), 327-338 (commitWalkin -- bare signature ending `;`; its 10-step sequence at 351-424 is numbered prose describing SQL/writes/table lookups, never a function body), 427-437 (CreateWalkinUserInput/createWalkinUser -- bare; the INSERT is a single inline-code SQL prose statement at 439-441, not fenced ts logic), 451-463 (CreateWalkinProfileInput/createWalkinProfile -- bare; INSERT described identically as inline prose at 465-466), 483-508 (WalkinMessageFields/formatWalkinConfirmMessage/formatWalkinOverrideMessage/ParseWalkinMessageResult/parseWalkinMessageFields -- all bare signatures; the canonical line format is a literal template shown as a fenced TEXT block (510-519), not TS code, and the parse rule is prose at 521-526), 550-554 (makeWalkinCommandHandler -- signature with `{ ... }` ellipsis body, established precedent from REQ-026/028/029's identical pattern, already PASSED), 580-586 (WALKIN_CONFIRM_PATTERN + makeWalkinConfirmCallbackHandler -- same ellipsis-body precedent), 624-630 (WALKIN_OVERRIDE_PATTERN + makeWalkinOverrideCallbackHandler -- same), 651-658 (makeWalkinCancelCallbackHandler -- ellipsis body only, `answerCallbackQuery`/`editMessageText` are direct grammY API calls with no branching logic, consistent with the ellipsis-handler precedent), 673-695 (walkin i18n Catalog key -- bare type). Grepped the full document for `if (`, `return <expr>;` outside outcome-literal returns, arithmetic, loops -- none found outside the accounted-for stub lines and the already-established ellipsis-handler precedent. VERDICT: clean, no implementation code.

2. DESIGN-TOKEN CHECK -- N/A, correctly justified (Sec13): the bot surface has no visual/CSS component; Telegram inline buttons and message text render plain text only. No color/spacing/typography reference appears anywhere in the document to check against docs/Design system for AI agents/tokens/tokens.css. Consistent with the identical, previously-accepted reasoning at REQ-016/017/018/028/029's gates.

3. MESSAGE-TEXT-AS-STATE-CARRIER -- CRITICAL SCRUTINY, the genuinely new mechanism:
   a. Server-authoritative content: ctx.callbackQuery.message is populated by Telegram's own servers from the message object as Telegram itself stores it -- it is not something the tapping client transmits independently of what Telegram already has on record. Grepped apps/bot/src for any prior use of ctx.callbackQuery.message.text (`callbackQuery\.message` -- no matches) -- this is a genuinely first use in this codebase, so there is no in-repo precedent to cross-check against, but grammY's Context/Api types mirror the Bot API's CallbackQuery.message field 1:1 with no client-supplied override path. Telegram's Bot API gives no mechanism for a non-bot client to alter a message's stored text -- only the bot itself can edit its own messages via editMessageText, and ordinary users have no 'edit another party's message' capability at all, let alone edit a bot's message. This makes the confirm message's text immutable between send and tap by construction, not merely by convention.

   b. Forgery scenario traced: an attacker cannot construct an arbitrary message carrying a `walkin:confirm:<eventId>` (or `walkin:override:<eventId>`) button, because only the bot's own SDK calls (reply with `reply_markup`) can attach that callback_data to a message in the first place -- a user-composed message has no mechanism to carry inline keyboard buttons pointing at the bot's own callback handlers. So there is no path by which content OR button could be attacker-crafted independently; the only messages a `walkin:confirm:*`/`walkin:override:*` handler will ever fire against are messages the bot itself sent in this exact flow, with content the bot itself rendered a moment earlier (Sec7.1's canonical formatter). Confirmed: the authorization gate (requireOrganizerForChapter, re-run at every tap, Sec4/Sec8.2 step 4/Sec8.3) is not what protects against content forgery here -- content forgery is structurally impossible given Telegram's actual message/callback model, a fact independent of whatever the authorization check does. The design's own Open Question 6 correctly names the one theoretical residual gap (a forwarded/edited copy of the SAME original message showing a stale Event: line) and correctly notes forwards strip buttons and only the bot can edit its own messages -- so even that residual gap does not admit attacker-authored content, only a stale-but-authentic Event: label with no acceptance criterion resting on it. No scenario exists where forged CONTENT bypasses the authorization gate, because content cannot be forged at all under Telegram's actual message model, and the eventId used for every write is sourced from callback_data (the tapped button), never from the re-parsed text (Sec7.1, explicit).

   c. Degradation on corruption/truncation: parseWalkinMessageFields (Sec7.1) returns `{ ok: false }` if any of the three fixed-prefix lines (`Name: `/`Company: `/`Phone: `) is not found, and Sec8.2 step 5 / Sec8.3 (inherited) route `!ok` to an explicit staleMessage refusal with NO write and no crash -- a clean, named failure path, not a silent proceed-with-corrupted-data or an unhandled exception. Telegram's message length cap (4096 chars) is far larger than this canonical 4-line message could plausibly reach given the field lengths a door-collected name/company/phone would realistically have, so truncation is not a realistic failure mode this design needed to additionally engineer around; the design's parse-or-refuse structure would degrade correctly even in that case regardless. VERDICT: this mechanism is genuinely sound, not merely asserted sound -- the immutability property rests on Telegram's actual message/callback architecture, not on an assumption the design merely declares.

4. EXISTING-PROFILE CONSENT QUESTION -- traced against S1's actual text ('nothing is kept without [consent to store data]... including walk-ins added at the door'). When matchedUserId is non-null (Sec6.2 step 3, table row 1), NO write to users or profiles occurs at all -- the existing row is reused exactly as-is. S1 is a property about consent preceding STORAGE; an existing profile can only exist in this system if consent was already recorded at some earlier point (createWalkinUser/recordConsent are the only two call sites that create a User row, both of which set consent_pd_at atomically with the row -- confirmed by grep of domain/consent.ts and domain/user.ts). Since this flow stores nothing new for a matched person (the door-supplied name/company are explicitly never written back into the existing profile, Sec6.2 step 3 row 1 and Open Question 2), there is no new storage event for S1 to gate -- correctly not re-requesting consent. This is the RIGHT read of S1, not a loophole: S1's negative case ('a walk-in path that skips the consent step because it is faster at the door') describes skipping consent for NEW data being stored, which does not occur here. One residual observation, non-blocking: the confirm message's consent statement (Sec7.2) is rendered before the phone-match lookup runs (matching only happens inside commitWalkin, reached after the tap), so an organizer sees consent wording even in the case that turns out to be an existing-profile match where no new consent-gated storage will occur. This is a minor copy/sequencing nicety, not a security defect (no invariant requires suppressing consent copy when the match outcome isn't yet known, and showing it does not create a false compliance record since S1 is satisfied by what is actually written, not by what copy was displayed) -- noted for the record, not a gate failure.

5. AC1 STRUCTURAL VERIFICATION (abandon-at-consent leaves zero rows) -- confirmed genuinely structural, not merely claimed: Sec8.1 step 7 (the command handler) performs no db write of any kind -- it only replies with a message. commitWalkin (Sec6, the only function in this design that writes to users/profiles/registrations) is called exclusively from Sec8.2 step 6 (confirm tap) and Sec8.3 step 6 (override tap) -- never from the command handler or from message construction. Sec1.1 explicitly states no state is persisted anywhere between the command and a Confirm tap. Traced: there is no code path from `/walkin` to any write that does not pass through an explicit Confirm or Confirm-override tap. AC1 holds structurally.

6. IDEMPOTENT RE-RUN / DOUBLE-TAP SAFETY (commitWalkin called twice across the flow, and the risk of a rapid double-tap on the SAME button) -- traced against Sec6.2's actual sequence, not assumed safe. Step 1 takes `SELECT ... FROM events WHERE id = $eventId FOR UPDATE` -- this locks the EVENT row for the transaction's duration, so two concurrent commitWalkin calls for the same event (whether confirm-then-override, or a genuine double-tap firing two overlapping callback_query updates for the same button) serialize on this lock: the second transaction blocks until the first commits. After the first commits, the second transaction's step 4 registration lookup will find the just-written row (admission='admitted', checked_in_at now non-null), and decideWalkinOutcome's step 4 (Sec5) routes this to `already-checked-in` -- Sec6.2 step 7 makes this a no-write outcome. Combined with `uq_registrations_event_user` (Sec0, confirmed pre-existing) making any conceivable insert-if-absent/update-if-present write target at most one row per (event,user) pair, a double-tap cannot produce two registration rows or two audit rows for the same person. This mirrors the exact discipline Sec6.1 cites from toggleCheckIn/performQrCheckIn/overrideAdmitAndCheckIn (REQ-028/029) and is correctly reused, not a new unverified claim.

7. ALL 6 ACs MAPPED (Sec11 table), independently cross-checked against the actual acceptance_criteria text in docs/agents/requirements.yaml (grep id: REQ-030, not paraphrased from the design's own summary): AC1 (zero new rows on abandon) -> Sec8.1 step 7 + Sec1.1, verified structural per item 5 above. AC2 (admitted + checked_in_at + manual, one flow) -> Sec6.2 step 9's single INSERT/UPDATE setting all three together, gated by Sec5 step 6 (seatsLeft>0 routes directly, no override interposed). AC3 (over-capacity requires confirmation; confirming writes exactly one audit_log row; dismissing creates no registration) -> Sec5 step 7/Sec6.2 step 7 (no write on needs-override-confirmation), Sec8.2 step 10 (override-offer message), Sec8.3 (override tap's single write + single audit row, verified per item 6), Sec8.4 (Dismiss never calls commitWalkin). AC4 (existing person reused, no duplicates) -> Sec3 (phone match) + Sec6.2 step 3 table (no users/profiles write when matched) + uq_registrations_event_user (Sec0) making the registration write itself insert-if-absent/update-if-present. AC5 (phone in no log line, no audit payload) -> Sec10, every writeAuditLog payload in Sec6.2 steps 8/9 is a fixed shape ({eventId, previousAdmission, source} or {eventId, source}) that structurally excludes phone; confirmed no log.* call site anywhere in the new handlers/domain functions receives the raw phone value as an argument. AC6 (EventStaff-not-organizer refused) -> Sec4 (requireOrganizerForChapter, never requireEventStaffForEvent) re-run independently at Sec8.1 step 5, Sec8.2 step 4, and Sec8.3's inherited step 4 -- three separate gate points, none skippable. No TBD/deferral language found anywhere; all 6 open questions (Sec12) each name a real residual gap with reasoned accept/defer, consistent with the precedent already accepted at REQ-016 through REQ-029's gates.

8. SCHEMA CLAIM (Sec0) -- design states no schema change needed; spot-checked against apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts precedent already independently verified at prior gates (users.tgId nullable+uniqueIndex from REQ-010, profiles' relaxed NOT NULLs from REQ-019-schema.md, uq_registrations_event_user and chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted from REQ-011/020/028/029) -- no new schema claim introduced here beyond what those prior, independently-verified reads already confirmed for the same columns/constraints. DATA-DESIGNER correctly does not run this cycle.

Verdict: PASS. Zero implementation code found. The message-text-as-state-carrier mechanism is genuinely sound: message content is server-authoritative and immutable between send and tap under Telegram's actual message/callback architecture (not merely asserted), content forgery is structurally impossible (not merely gated by authorization as a backstop), and corruption/truncation degrades to a clean, named refusal rather than a crash or silent proceed. The existing-profile consent question is correctly resolved -- no new storage occurs for a matched person, so S1 does not require re-consent, with one minor non-blocking copy-sequencing observation recorded for the audit trail. AC1's zero-rows-on-abandon property is structurally verified, not merely claimed. The override's idempotent re-run is protected against double-registration by the event-row lock serializing concurrent commitWalkin calls plus uq_registrations_event_user, not by any new dedup mechanism this design would have needed to invent. All 6 ACs map to concrete design elements, independently cross-checked against the actual requirements.yaml text.

context.verification_notes: Confirmed via grep that ctx.callbackQuery.message.text is a genuinely first use in this codebase (no prior call sites). Confirmed via grep that domain/consent.ts's recordConsent and domain/user.ts's User row shape are the only prior consent_pd_at write sites, supporting the existing-profile-skip-consent reasoning. Confirmed the 6 acceptance_criteria in docs/agents/requirements.yaml (lines 1557-1563) match Sec11's mapping table verbatim in substance, not paraphrased. Confirmed apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts's relevant columns/constraints were already independently verified pre-existing at prior gates (REQ-010/011/019-schema/020/028/029) -- no new schema claim introduced.
